title: 2025-09-22 Weekly Cycle Edit Proposal
author: 0xldr
summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Update Near-Term Logic Regarding Perpetual Exposures - Increases RRC for Ethena exposures, adds near-term logic for Superstate, and establishes aggregate exposure limits. Add Ecosystem Dispute Resolution Process - Defines the initial process for resolution of disputes regarding Ecosystem Accords. Correct Typographical Error - Corrects a minor spelling error. Update Near-Term Logic Regarding Perpetual Exposures Replace the subdocuments of A.3.3.2.1.1.1.2.1 - Near-Term Treatment (Portal) / A.3.3 - Near-Term Treatment (GitHub) to read as follows: A.3.3 - Ethena (Core) - The near-term treatment for Ethena is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital (Core) - Ethena Exposures consist of Direct Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures) and Indirect Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures). The Instance Financial RRC for Ethena Exposures is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Direct Ethena Exposures (Core) - Direct Ethena Exposures are exposures from directly holding USDe and sUSDe. Direct Ethena Exposures have a 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. A.3.3 - Indirect Ethena Exposures (Core) - Indirect Ethena Exposures are exposures from lending against Ethena related assets through lending markets. Indirect Ethena Exposures have Instance Financial RRC as specified in the documents herein. For Indirect Ethena Exposure through lending markets, only the portion of the exposure to the lending market that is backed by Ethena related assets is subject to the Instance Financial RRC Ratio specified in the documents herein. The Instance Financial RRC Ratio for the remaining portion of the exposure is calculated based on the nature of the assets backing the exposure. A.3.3 - Lending Ethena Related Assets Against Ethena Related Collateral (Core) - For Ethena related assets lent against Ethena related collateral (e.g. lending USDe or sUSDe against PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe), the Instance Financial RRC Ratio is 3%. A.3.3 - Lending Non-Ethena Related Assets Against Ethena Related Collateral (Core) - For non-Ethena related assets lent against Ethena related collateral (e.g. lending USDC against PT-USDe or PT-sUSDe), the Instance Financial RRC Ratio is 4%. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limits (Core) - The documents herein define aggregate exposure limits applicable to Ethena. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Ethena Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Ethena Exposures (see A.3.3 - Ethena Required Risk Capital) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit is 1,500,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Ethena Exposures that would cause the Ethena Aggregate Exposure to exceed the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If the Ethena Aggregate Exposure exceeds the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct Prime Agents to sell Ethena Exposures to reduce the Ethena Aggregate Exposure below the Ethena Aggregate Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Superstate (Core) - The near-term treatment for Superstate is specified in the documents herein. A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital (Core) - Superstate Exposures are exposures from holding USCC. Superstate Exposures have a 3% Instance Financial RRC Ratio. A.3.3 - Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limits (Core) - The documents herein define aggregate exposure limits applicable to Superstate Exposures. A.3.3 - Superstate Aggregate Exposure (Core) - Superstate Aggregate Exposure is the sum of Superstate Exposures (see A.3.3 - Superstate Required Risk Capital) across all Prime Agents in the Sky Ecosystem. A.3.3 - Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit (Core) - The Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit is 500,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Prohibition On Investments That Would Cause Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit To Be Exceeded (Core) - No Prime Agent may make an investment in Superstate Exposures that would cause the Superstate Aggregate Exposure to exceed the Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Sale Of Investments When Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit Is Exceeded (Core) - If the Superstate Aggregate Exposure exceeds the Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit, then the Core Council may direct Prime Agents to sell Superstate Exposures to reduce the Superstate Aggregate Exposure below the Superstate Aggregate Exposure Limit. A.3.3 - Superstate Deployment Limits (Core) - The documents herein define the deployment limits applicable to Superstate Exposures. A.3.3 - Superstate Initial Deployment Limit (Core) - The Initial Deployment is the first deployment of capital by a Prime Agent into Superstate Exposures. The Initial Deployment may not exceed 20,000,000 USDS. A.3.3 - Superstate Subsequent Deployment Limits (Core) - Subsequent Deployments are deployments of capital by a Prime Agent into Superstate Exposures after its Initial Deployment (see A.3.3 - Superstate Initial Deployment Limit). Each Subsequent Deployment may not exceed 50,000,000 USDS and requires approval from BA Labs on behalf of the Core Council. Add Ecosystem Dispute Resolution Process Replace A.2.9 - Ecosystem Accords (Portal) / A.2.8 - Ecosystem Accords (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - Ecosystem Accords (Article) - This Article governs Ecosystem Accords, agreements between actors in the Sky Ecosystem that are enforceable by Sky Governance. Add new subdocuments of A.2.9 - Ecosystem Accords (Portal) / A.2.8 - Ecosystem Accords (GitHub) . These documents should be located directly before A.2.9.1 - List Of Active Ecosystem Accords (Portal) / A.2.8 - A1 - Ecosystem Accords - List Of Active Ecosystem Accords (GitHub) to read as follows: A.2.10 - A1 - Dispute Resolution (Section) - This Section defines the process for resolving disputes regarding Ecosystem Accords. A.2.10 - Dispute Resolution By Core Council (Core) - Disputes regarding Ecosystem Accords are resolved by the Core Council as specified in the documents herein. A.2.10 - Roles (Core) - The documents herein define the respective roles of Core GovOps and the Core Facilitator in resolving disputes. A.2.10 - Role Of Core GovOps (Core) - Core GovOps manages the overall dispute resolution process, including establishing communication channels for dispute resolution, communicating with the parties, and gathering and analyzing information relating to the dispute. A.2.10 - Role Of Core Facilitator (Core) - The Core Facilitator decides how the dispute is ultimately resolved. The Core Facilitator is isolated from the parties to maintain impartiality. The Core Facilitator exclusively reviews the information prepared by Core GovOps and delivers a decision to Core GovOps, which communicates it to the parties. A.2.10 - Process Definition (Core) - The documents herein define the process for resolving disputes. A.2.10 - Dispute Intake (Core) - The documents herein define the process for dispute intake for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Formal Request For Dispute Resolution (Core) - The dispute resolution process begins with an actor in the Sky Ecosystem requesting formal dispute resolution from Core GovOps. A.2.10 - Preliminary Determination Of Reasonableness By Core GovOps (Core) - After receiving the request for dispute resolution, Core GovOps makes a brief preliminary determination regarding whether the request is reasonable (i.e. not vexatious or frivolous), within three (3) working days. A.2.10 - Handling Of Unreasonable Requests (Core) - If Core GovOps determines that the request for dispute resolution is not reasonable, it will inform the actor who submitted the request accordingly, providing their reasons. In this case, there is no further action. A.2.10 - Handling Of Reasonable Requests (Core) - If Core GovOps makes a determination that the request is reasonable, then Core GovOps formally begins the dispute resolution process by notifying all relevant parties that the process is about to begin. The notifications to each party will outline the process to be followed, including relevant steps and timeframes that the party should be aware of. A.2.10 - Presentation Of Arguments (Core) - The documents herein define the process for the presentation of arguments for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Statement Of Problem (Core) - The party that initiated the dispute resolution process has five (5) working days from the formal initiation of the process to submit a Statement of Problem, laying out the facts they consider relevant to the dispute and the issues related to the Atlas as they see them. A.2.10 - Statement Of Response (Core) - Core GovOps provides the Statement of Problem to the other party/parties. They have five (5) working days to submit a Statement of Response, which sets out their perspective on the relevant facts and issues in the dispute. A.2.10 - Statement Of Rebuttal (Core) - Core GovOps provides the Statement of Response to the party that initiated the dispute resolution process. They have three (3) working days to submit a Statement of Rebuttal. A.2.10 - Decision (Core) - The documents herein define the decision process for dispute resolution. A.2.10 - Analysis By Core GovOps (Core) - Core GovOps prepares a confidential analysis of the dispute for the Core Facilitator. This analysis must include a summary of all relevant facts as far as it is possible to ascertain, clear identification of any areas of factual ambiguity or disagreement between the parties, a structured presentation of the arguments in favor of each party, and a recommendation if Core GovOps believes one conclusion is clearly supported by the facts. A.2.10 - Adjudication By Core Facilitator (Core) - The Core Facilitator reviews the analysis prepared by Core GovOps along with the arguments presented by the parties and reaches a decision within three (3) working days. The Core Facilitator must draft a decision setting out relevant facts and the core reasoning of their decision. In doing so, the Core Facilitator is free to adopt arguments presented by the parties, by Core GovOps, or to advance their own analysis. A.2.10 - Release Of Decision (Core) - The Core Facilitator communicates their decision to Core GovOps. Core GovOps communicates the decision to all related parties. A.2.10 - Publication Of Decision (Core) - The Core Facilitator publishes the decision on the Sky Forum and updates the A.2.10 - Dispute Resolutions Active Data document in the Atlas, redacting any confidential information as needed. A.2.10 - Dispute Resolution Recording (Active Data Controller) - Resolutions of disputes involving Ecosystem Accords are defined as Active Data in A.2.10 - Dispute Resolutions. The Active Data is updated as follows: The Responsible Party is the Core Facilitator. The Update Process must follow the protocol for ‘Direct Edit’. The Accessibility Facilitators then pay the Accessibility Reward from the Accessibility Reward Controller Wallet located on the Ethereum Mainnet at 0x05F471262d15EECA4059DadE070e5BEd509a4e73 within seven (7) days of the end of every month. The balance of this wallet may be topped up to 3 million USDS. This funding is subject to an Executive Vote.
